  • enacted to protect women from domestic violence within domestic relationships.
  • b. Objective: Its primary objective is to provide effective legal protection and accessible remedies
  • for women experiencing domestic violence.
  • c. Definition of domestic violence: Section 3 recognizes physical, sexual, verbal, emotional and
  • economic abuse as forms of domestic violence.
  • d. Persons protected: The Act protects an aggrieved woman who is, or has been, in a domestic
  • relationship with the respondent and alleges domestic violence.
  • e. Right to reside: Section 17 recognizes an aggrieved woman's right to reside in the shared
  • household, subject to the provisions of the Act.
  • f. Protection orders: Under Section 18, a Magistrate may prohibit the respondent from
  • committing domestic violence or engaging in specified harmful acts.
  • g. Residence orders: Section 19 allows the Magistrate to issue appropriate residence-related
  • orders to protect the aggrieved woman.
  • h. Monetary relief: Section 20 provides for monetary relief to meet expenses and losses resulting
  • from domestic violence, including maintenance where applicable.
  • i. Custody orders: Under Section 21, the Magistrate may grant temporary custody of children to
  • the aggrieved woman and regulate visitation where appropriate.
  • j. Compensation orders: Section 22 allows compensation and damages for injuries, including
  • mental torture and emotional distress caused by domestic violence.
  • k. Interim and ex parte orders
  • l. Role of Protection Officers.
  • m. Role of service providers.
  • n. Legal assistance and support.
  • o. Role of social workers to identify abuse, assess safety risks, provide psychosocial support.

questions.question: Evaluate the legislations related to women and children and the legal safeguards? (E)
questions.solution_html:
• a. Definition: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 is an Indian law
  • enacted to protect women from domestic violence within domestic relationships.
  • b. Objective: Its primary objective is to provide effective legal protection and accessible remedies
  • for women experiencing domestic violence.
  • c. Definition of domestic violence: Section 3 recognizes physical, sexual, verbal, emotional and
  • economic abuse as forms of domestic violence.
  • d. Persons protected: The Act protects an aggrieved woman who is, or has been, in a domestic
  • relationship with the respondent and alleges domestic violence.
  • e. Right to reside: Section 17 recognizes an aggrieved woman's right to reside in the shared
  • household, subject to the provisions of the Act.
  • f. Protection orders: Under Section 18, a Magistrate may prohibit the respondent from
  • committing domestic violence or engaging in specified harmful acts.
  • g. Residence orders: Section 19 allows the Magistrate to issue appropriate residence-related
  • orders to protect the aggrieved woman.
  • h. Monetary relief: Section 20 provides for monetary relief to meet expenses and losses resulting
  • from domestic violence, including maintenance where applicable.
  • i. Custody orders: Under Section 21, the Magistrate may grant temporary custody of children to
  • the aggrieved woman and regulate visitation where appropriate.
  • j. Compensation orders: Section 22 allows compensation and damages for injuries, including
  • mental torture and emotional distress caused by domestic violence.
  • k. Interim and ex parte orders
  • l. Role of Protection Officers.
  • m. Role of service providers.
  • n. Legal assistance and support.
  • o. Role of social workers to identify abuse, assess safety risks, provide psychosocial support.
